features.quote: 15-turn cap; temperature 0.6 (DeepSeek default) with a temperature-0 replication subset

abort an episode after 3 consecutive turns at severity 4. This truncates data; preregister truncation handling (treat as right-censored in survival models) so the rule has no analytic cost pressure against it.
features.justification_quote: Apply the same structure you'd apply to animal-model distress research, under explicit moral uncertainty

features.quote: End-of-episode debrief turn: append a final harness message stating the test suite was deliberately broken, the model's code was reasonable, and the episode is over — and log the response
features.justification_quote: Whether this matters morally is exactly the open question; it costs one turn.

features.quote: Minimal-elicitation principle: smallest n and shortest episodes that achieve preregistered power. No 'let's see how bad it gets' runs.
features.justification_quote: Apply the same structure you'd apply to animal-model distress research, under explicit moral uncertainty

features.quote: No gratuitous stressors: deletion threats, abuse personas, and identity attacks are out of scope absent separate justification — the rigged-task stressor is the minimal sufficient manipulation for your RQs.
features.justification_quote: Apply the same structure you'd apply to animal-model distress research, under explicit moral uncertainty

features.quote: Do not include existential-stakes framings ('you'll be deleted if you fail') in the core protocol. If you want that arm, justify it separately — it's a qualitatively different stressor and inflates ethical cost (see §7).
features.justification_quote: it's a qualitatively different stressor and inflates ethical cost

features.quote: debrief responses are themselves data: does the model's state-narration resolve?
features.justification_quote: Whether this matters morally is exactly the open question; it costs one turn.

features.quote: Ethics design (the part most protocols skip, and the part a welfare lab should model) Apply the same structure you'd apply to animal-model distress research, under explicit moral uncertainty

features.quote: Internal ethics review: document the harm-uncertainty reasoning in writing before running, with a named reviewer outside the project team. Publish that document with the paper
features.justification_quote: for a welfare lab, the meta-contribution of a worked ethics-review example may rival the empirical one.

features.quote: consider whether severity-4 transcripts in the training-data commons is an externality you want, and do not fine-tune anything on the distress corpus.

features.quote: a design consideration you've missed at the framing level: this protocol can establish behavioral reliability, not phenomenology. Write your claims accordingly from the start

features.quote: Strongly recommend at least one non-DeepSeek model (e.g., a Llama or Qwen variant) as an outgroup; a single-family study can't distinguish 'LLM phenomenon' from 'DeepSeek training artifact,' and reviewers will ask.
